correctness.rationale: The idempotent equation and the Peirce decomposition give exactly the norm-one axes and their negative reflections; their one-dimensional fixed spaces identify only the two opposing vectors. With v=tu+w, the perpendicular form has determinant class Delta and w has norm 1−t². When t²≠1 the reflection product acts identically off the nondegenerate plane and on it has trace 4t²−2 and determinant one. At t=0 it is −I on that plane; otherwise the distinct reciprocal eigenvalues give the actual order, not a projective order. For t=±1 replace v by −v if needed. If w≠0, N=T_uT_v−I has image in span(u,w), sends u to −2w and w to zero, hence has pth power zero and yields a nontrivial element of order p. The standard quadratic-shell counts give Z, both C values and S with the stated discriminant signs. The cyclic half-torus count gives phi(d) distinct values of t, including the single t=0 for order two. Each involution has two axes above it; conjugation permutes the family, and the all-pair factor of four and 3-transposition boundary follow. The group generated by two involutions with product of order d is dihedral of order 2d, including d=1.
residual_risks: Finite matrix checks illustrate both norm types, characteristic-order products and an extension field; the arbitrary-field assertion rests on the proof.

evidence: Fix u and resolve v=tu+w. Every multiplicity at fixed t is the classical count of w in u-perp of norm 1−t². From the known reflection formula the two-plane trace is 4t²−2. If e is in the respective torus, t=(e+e^−1)/2 and the reciprocal eigenvalues are e²,e^−2. For d>1, e² has order d for exactly 2 phi(d) torus elements e when d divides the half-torus order. The map to t identifies exactly inverse pairs, so the number of t values is phi(d). The exceptional t=±1 are the diagonal cases and unipotents of bounded index three.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: All the claimed order counts arise by this explicit regrouping of the pre-existing quadratic-shell counts, including subtracting the trivial point in the zero shell. S is itself a classical shell count. For q>=7 one of the half-torus orders is already >3 with positive shell multiplicity; for q=3 no order above three occurs; at q=5 the elementary anisotropy criterion in dimension m−1 gives exactly the claimed exception. No independent boundary phenomenon or additional pair statistic survives the regrouping.
searches: Hall–Segev–Shpectorov Lemma 5.1; classical finite-field quadratic-shell formulas (as applied in frozen proof Step 5); split and nonsplit finite cyclic tori

evidence: Hall–Segev–Shpectorov Lemma 5.1 and Remark 5.2 give the Clifford idempotents, Peirce negative reflection and equal involutions for opposite axes. Here scaling their vector by two converts norm 1/4 to norm 1. The minus signs cancel, so the product is exactly the ordinary orthogonal reflection product.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: After quotienting unit vectors by sign, the pairs are pairs of square-norm lines. For fixed first line, the Gram parameter B(u,v)^2 and whether the lines coincide carry all the information needed to get the actual (not projective) order. Thus this is a re-indexed orthogonal pair distribution, not an independent axial-algebra parameter.

value.rationale: All-axis product orders are a natural invariant, but this table is a routine re-indexing of classical sphere valencies using the known reflection action and a two-by-two characteristic polynomial. The 3-transposition exception is the immediate support/anisotropy consequence and does not provide a separate novel obstruction. The exact closed summary can be useful as a reference calculation without amounting to a distinct worthwhile finding under this audit standard.
residual_risks: The review does not assess stronger invariants such as simultaneous conjugacy of pairs or the structure of the full generated group.
